## Completion Verification Report

**Overall verdict: FAIL**

All 8 child stories are now closed (6 were closed in the session handoff; 744b and d6d1 subsequently closed per their ticket records). Seven of the eight Acceptance Criteria are met. One AC item is not met.

---

### AC-by-AC findings

**AC1 — v2 IR JSON Schema + v1->v2 migrate shim + linter (cycles legal only via declared loop frames); coverage guard: ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json` exists (`additionalProperties:false`, branch/loop/map constructs, mandatory `max_iterations`).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/migrate.py` exists with a v1→v2 shim and golden round-trip test reference.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint.py` + `lint_refs.py` implement frame-scoped reference checks.
- Child b44a is closed with a code-reviewer sign-off.

**AC2 — Interpreter: conditionals/loops/map; iteration-keyed markers; mandatory max_iterations; replay tests: ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py` implements the recursive v2 worklist interpreter.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` wires the run-state recorder.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` holds the iteration-keyed WORKFLOW_STEP slot.
- Child dbc6 is closed with independently-run real-recorder tests and the production bug fix confirmed.

**AC3 — Bounded-concurrent fan-out: parallel agent calls + serialized event commits; deterministic replay preserved; Burr tripwire relaxed NARROWLY for the map path only (recorded): ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/map_fanout.py` exists and carries the recorded rationale for the narrow tripwire relaxation.
- Child 8d8e is closed with concurrency stress tests.

**AC4 — PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam; FS+MCP+custom tools; structured output via NativeOutput/PromptedOutput; validate + bounded retry; parity bar met before LangGraph drop: ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` contains `class PydanticAIRunner` (line 125).
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py` and `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` exist.
- Child 7d58 is closed with defined non-inferiority parity bar; child d6d1 confirmed cutover after parity validation.

**AC5 — LangChain/LangGraph/langchain-mcp-adapters removed; tracing via [tracing] OTel->Langfuse, optional: ✅ MET (with documented in-scope relaxation)**

- `search_files("langchain", "src/")` returns no matches — the stack is fully removed.
- `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py` implements `setup_tracing()` as no-op without keys/extra.
- Child d6d1 is closed. Note: "trace fidelity verified" was explicitly amended to "wired-but-unverified" per an in-session decision by the ticket author (live Langfuse creds required); this is a documented, acknowledged relaxation, not an undiscovered gap.

**AC6 — Structured-output reliability layers 1-4 implemented; thinking+extraction split where needed; stop_reason handling; second-interpreter LLM removed: ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` implements the 4-layer stack (NativeOutput/PromptedOutput + json-repair + Pydantic validators + bounded retry + stop_reason handling).
- Child 1268 is closed.

**AC7 — bpmn-js editor + IR<->BPMN serializer with a registered `rebar` moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures (ids, agent metadata, multi-instance survive); visual format never committed: ✅ MET**

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/bpmn.py` (serializer), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/rebar.moddle.json` (descriptor), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` (launcher + save server) all exist.
- Child 00da closed (serializer + moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures); child 744b closed (bpmn-js editor, after human browser validation gate).

**AC8 — docs reference the 3 de-risk POCs: ❌ NOT MET**

The 3 POC files exist under `docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/`:
- `engine_interpreter_poc.py`
- `runtime_pydanticai_poc.py`
- `visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs`

However, searching the entire repository (`search_files` across `.`) finds:
- `engine_interpreter_poc.py`: Referenced only in `tests/unit/workflow/test_interpreter_v2.py` (a test-module docstring), not in any documentation file.
- `runtime_pydanticai_poc.py`: Not referenced anywhere outside itself.
- `visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs`: Not referenced anywhere outside itself.

No documentation file (`docs/*.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/workflow-editor.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, etc.) explicitly mentions or links to these 3 POC files. The `docs/experiments/README.md` covers earlier plan-validation experiments but not the workflow-remediation POCs. `src/rebar/llm/bpmn.py` says "The de-risk POC proved..." without naming the file; `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` references the `structured-output-research.md` research document (not one of the 3 POCs). The AC requires documentation to reference all 3 de-risk POCs; two of the three are unreferenced anywhere.

---

**Summary:** 7 of 8 Acceptance Criteria are met. AC8 ("docs reference the 3 de-risk POCs") is not met: `runtime_pydanticai_poc.py` and `visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs` are not referenced in any documentation or source file outside themselves, and no documentation file references all 3 POC files.

PASS 1 — T1 (Prior-art / novel-architecture justification, OVERLAY): PASS / not-applicable — no findings.

T1's bright-lines (external integration, unfamiliar dependency, security/auth, novel architectural pattern, perf/scalability target, migration) do not fire for this plan. It is an incremental extension of the EXISTING, documented workflow editor and engine, not a novel architecture:

- Dependencies already vendored & in use — bpmn-js, bpmn-js-properties-panel, bpmn-moddle, the registered `rebar` moddle descriptor, and the Python IR↔BPMN round-trip (docs/workflow-editor.md). No new dependency is introduced; the plan says "confirm + extend only as needed."
- Prior-art consideration already on record in this area — `bpmn-auto-layout` was evaluated and rejected with a documented rationale (docs/workflow-editor.md "A readable layout").
- The constructs being made editable pre-exist in the engine: the `batch` step + prompt-library-backed `criteria` list with `when` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py `_run_batch`, executor.py `BatchRunner`/`DefaultBatchRunner`, lint.py, schema.py; sample in examples/review_skeleton.yaml) and the prompt step `if:`/`when` overlay predicate. The editor's config-carrying mechanism (`<rebar:Config>` extension + moddle registration) and properties-panel custom provider also pre-exist.
- No unverified capability assertions: the load-bearing claims (the e6d9 editor invariant — clean git diffs + schema-validated round-trip; moddle-faithful round-trip) map to existing, documented code/tests.

Per the criterion's ANTI-FP guidance, a well-trodden pattern needs no prior-art search and T1 is not-applicable when no bright-line fires. Affirmation: criteria T1 satisfied (not-applicable, clean).

comments.body:
PLAN REVIEW · PASS 1 · [T8] LLM/prompt structural-completeness probe (overlay) — VERDICT: CLEAN (no findings).

This epic defines an LLM/agent system (3 agentic reviewers + eval specs + deterministic-scorer registry + a context-injection live solver), so the T8 overlay applies. I tool-probed each structural-gap class against the codebase and found every one satisfied at the plan level:

- (a) No undefined-but-referenced enum/schema vocabulary. The "deterministic-scorer registry" AC requires every scorer NAME used by the packaged specs to map to an implemented pure function. The scorer-name vocabulary is concretely defined: existing packaged specs name them (src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-quality.eval.yaml:19,22 emits_valid_review_result/cites_real_paths; plan-review-finder.eval.yaml:19,22,27; plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml:16,19,26; plan-review-isf-finder.eval.yaml:15,18,21), and the 3 NEW specs' scorer names are an explicit authoring deliverable (child rink-cloud-gum Phase-1 + Phase-2.1). The scorer TYPE enum (deterministic | llm-judge) is fully defined and enforced in validate_scorer (src/rebar/llm/eval.py:120-166). This is a build deliverable, not a referenced-but-undefined enum.

- (b) Processing protocol co-located with the schema that needs it. The grader-discipline decision rules (cross-family judge, gates:false for judges, at_least(k) over epochs, coverage threshold, pinned/dated grader) are co-located with the spec-validation surface they govern (validate_eval_spec / validate_scorer / parse_gate, eval.py:107-223). The AC mirrors these rules exactly (cross-family judge gates:false, at_least(k) over explicit epochs, coverage threshold, non-empty gold_set), so the executor's rule and the schema are not split.

- (c) No counter/state increment with ambiguous placement. at_least(k)-over-epochs (eval.py:229-231) and coverage = scored/total (eval.py:234-240) are precisely defined; the unsatisfiable-k guard (eval.py:207-208) closes the only edge.

- (d) A fallback for an incomplete/failed sub-step is specified. The agentic reviewers carry an explicit failed-sub-step fallback in-prompt ("after a bounded search, you cannot find evidence ... treat it as NOT MET — never assume", reviewers/completion_verifier.md:88-89), and the eval AC names BOTH branches of the repo-tool fallback ("stubbed OR fixture-backed repo tools"). The deeper "what if a reviewer tool call escapes the fixture corpus" detail is reasonably deferred to the task child (rink-cloud-gum Phase-2.2/2.4), not an under-specification of the plan criterion itself.

- (e) No instruction-locality/pink-elephant antipattern; referenced agents/skills exist and are fully specified (tool-verified). The 3 agentic reviewers the eval seam targets all exist and are fully specified — src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md (untrusted-input guard, bounded tool budget, structured completion_verdict, read-only constraints), ticket_quality.md, spec_alignment.md. run_eval()'s NotImplementedError stub is correctly characterized by the plan as an unwired-but-present harness (eval.py:319-351), matching the AC's "no longer raises NotImplementedError" deliverable.

affirmations: [T8] — no undefined-but-referenced scorer/enum vocabulary; grader-discipline protocol co-located with the spec schema; at_least(k)/coverage counters unambiguously placed; failed-sub-step fallback specified (reviewer NOT-MET default + stubbed/fixture repo-tool branch); referenced agentic reviewers exist and are fully specified (tool-verified). compiled_state.description:
# Workflow engine v2: declarative IR + thin interpreter + provider-agnostic runtime + visual editing

## Context

Split out of the remediation epic 6f2d (soupy-spool-revel) per the deep-design brainstorm (session log
ad3f-2d99-6d41-40e6 "boom-demon-jug"). The brainstorm established that "remediation" is really a
re-architecture of the workflow engine; THIS epic owns the BUILD. 6f2d retains remediation-on-top (docs,
migrating existing reviewers onto this engine, prompts, eval coverage, cleanup, visual+eval review,
intent-alignment) and depends_on this epic. Every decision is grounded in 4 deep-research rounds + codebase
spikes + 3 passing de-risk POCs under docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/ (REFERENCE, not deliverables).

## What we are building (4 parts)

- **Declarative IR (git source of truth):** one YAML/JSON file per workflow; steps are deterministic
  (`uses:` an INTERNAL registered op) or agentic (`prompt:` an LLM step); control flow (conditional
  branches, bounded loops, map/fan-out) expressed as DATA; stable step ids. Evolves v1 GitHub-Actions YAML.
- **Thin synchronous interpreter (engine):** run-state on rebar's EVENT LOG (genuine reuse —
  WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP events on the target ticket, same reducer/commit/push); iteration-keyed
  idempotency markers; mandatory max_iterations; control-flow state derived from recorded outputs
  (replay-correctness discipline the engine POC proved). BOUNDED-CONCURRENT fan-out: parallel LLM calls,
  serialized commits (decision: included in v1).
- **Provider-agnostic agent runtime behind the existing Runner seam:** Pydantic AI, REPLACING
  LangChain/LangGraph (sole justification — native Langfuse tracing — is obsolete; Langfuse is OTel-native).
  Runs single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents (filesystem + MCP + custom rebar-op tools). Tracing via
  OTel -> Langfuse, dev/maintenance only (clients pay nothing).
- **Ephemeral visual editor:** bpmn-js (constrained BPMN metamodel — NOT draw.io's free-form canvas, which
  would allow edits that don't map back). A thin IR<->BPMN serializer (bpmn-moddle + a registered `rebar`
  moddle descriptor) projects the IR for editing and round-trips back; the visual format is NEVER committed
  (auto-layout on open).

## Structured-output reliability (output feeds deterministic steps — reliability is key)

Retire the second-interpreter LLM (a recognized anti-pattern). Layered stack (research-grounded):
1. Provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported (OpenAI strict ~100% vs <40%;
   Gemini responseSchema; **Anthropic native structured outputs now GA**) via Pydantic AI NativeOutput; else
   PromptedOutput cross-provider.
2. Deterministic tolerant parse of near-miss output (json-repair) — no LLM.
3. Pydantic validation + normalizing validators (numeric/length bounds HERE, not in the JSON Schema, to stay
   inside Anthropic's strict-grammar subset).
4. Bounded SAME-model retry feeding the validation error back (Pydantic AI retries={'output': 2}; raise the
   default budget of 1).
Handle Anthropic stop_reason in {refusal, max_tokens}; for steps needing extended thinking, SPLIT reasoning
and structured extraction into two steps (thinking is a tradeoff vs forced structured output).

## Dependencies

- Reuse: event-sourced git store (run-state), git-canonical prompt library, Inspect AI eval seam, Runner seam.
- Add (runtime, light): pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,...] (~41 pkgs vs LangGraph ~80-110); provider SDKs;
  json-repair; OTel exporter ([tracing]) -> Langfuse.
- Drop: langchain, langgraph, langchain-mcp-adapters.
- Add (edit-time ONLY, out-of-process): bpmn-js (browser editor) + bpmn-moddle (MIT serializer). NOT runtime.
- Build (the only custom code): IR schema+linter (low risk); interpreter (moderate, justified by
  event-sourcing); Pydantic-AI Runner adapter (low); IR<->BPMN serializer (moderate, bounded — bpmn-moddle +
  one descriptor + round-trip fixtures; POC-validated).

## How it meets the invariants
- I1 human visual edit incl. loops/conditionals: bpmn-js (constrained metamodel) + round-trip serializer.
- I2 LLM edit+validate: lean schema'd IR; atomic id-keyed edit ops + schema + linter validation.
- I3 git-stored, clean diff NOT required: only the IR is committed; visual format ephemeral.
- I4 light runtime / heavy edit-deps OK: interpreter is stdlib; agent runtime lazy-loaded for agent steps;
  visual editor out-of-process.
- Cross-provider (hard req): Pydantic AI provider-agnostic, NO per-provider code; Anthropic-only rejected.
- Tool-using agents (FS+MCP+rebar ops): native to Pydantic AI (validated).
- Deterministic step logic INTERNAL-only (registry not exposed via CLI/MCP).
- Don't-build-unique-engine is EARNED: every off-the-shelf engine (DBOS/Restate/Spiff) owns its run-state and
  conflicts with event-sourcing; standard formats (BPMN/ASL) carry impedance > a lean IR.

## De-risk POCs (all PASS; docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/)
- engine_interpreter_poc.py: replay exactly-once across ALL crash points (deepest risk retired).
- runtime_pydanticai_poc.py: cross-provider integration validated; Claude thinking+structured-output 400
  reproduced AND mitigated (PromptedOutput); dep weight 41.
- visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs: IR<->BPMN round-trip preserves ids / multi-instance / agent metadata.

## Known limitations
- We own/maintain the interpreter (replay correctness is subtle — POC found+fixed one bug; contained by the
  state-discipline rule + tests).
- IR<->BPMN serializer is bespoke and bounded by BPMN's vocabulary (our IR must map onto BPMN).
- Agent-step config richness in the canvas is limited (edit flow visually, prompts in text).
- Pydantic AI is young (2.0 beta incoming) — contained by the strict swappable Runner seam.
- OTel->Langfuse token/cost attribute mapping is a known soft spot (analytics, not span structure).
- Cross-provider COMPLETION proven on Anthropic; OpenAI/Google billing-blocked (integration validated).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] v2 IR JSON Schema + v1->v2 migrate shim + linter (cycles legal only via declared loop frames); coverage guard.
- [ ] Interpreter: conditionals/loops/map; iteration-keyed (run_id,step_id,iteration) markers; mandatory
      max_iterations; replay tests (kill mid-run -> replay from events -> no double effects).
- [ ] Bounded-concurrent fan-out: parallel agent calls + serialized event commits; deterministic replay
      preserved; Burr tripwire relaxed NARROWLY for the map path only (recorded).
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam; FS+MCP+custom tools; structured output via NativeOutput/
      PromptedOutput (NOT forced-tool ToolOutput); validate + bounded retry; parallel-run-and-diff vs the old
      LangGraph path to the DEFINED PARITY BAR (child 7d58: non-inferiority on the eval corpus — validity >= v1,
      per-criterion verdict-agreement >= 95% + zero decision flips, recall/false-accept within +/-2pp) before
      cutover; the bar gates the LangGraph drop.
- [ ] LangChain/LangGraph/langchain-mcp-adapters removed; tracing via [tracing] OTel->Langfuse, optional.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability layers 1-4 implemented; thinking+extraction split where needed;
      stop_reason handling; second-interpreter LLM removed.
- [ ] bpmn-js editor + IR<->BPMN serializer with a registered `rebar` moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures
      (ids, agent metadata, multi-instance survive); visual format never committed.
- [ ] docs reference the 3 de-risk POCs.
- [ ] v2 declarative IR (steps + conditionals + loops + map) with a JSON Schema + linter, agent-editable.
- [ ] Thin interpreter executing it with run-state on the event log, deterministic resume/replay, and
- [ ] Agent runtime swapped to provider-agnostic Pydantic AI behind the Runner seam; LangGraph dropped.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability stack (native/strict + tolerant parse + validators + bounded retry); the
- [ ] Human visual view+edit via bpmn-js over an ephemeral IR<->BPMN projection.
